title: orchestrate-presubmit-sanitizer-and-dep-heatmap
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add lightweight presubmit sanitizer to reduce CI I/O and introduce dependency-heatmap telemetry to prioritize dep updates. No user-facing API changes. Migrate teams to opt-in by feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit lanes are increasingly noisy — heavy toolchain fetches and broad test matrices create flakiness and slow feedback. Separately, dependabot/renovate churn is hard to prioritize because we lack visibility into which transitive changes actually affect runtime paths. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: (1) a presubmit-sanitizer runtime that trims and gates presubmit toolchain work per-change, and (2) a dep-heatmap telemetry pipeline that surfaces dependency churn impact so we can prioritize rotations and reduce blind upgrades.

Summary of changes (commits):
- 9c8f2b3: introduce presubmit-sanitizer service and feature-flag scaffold
- 4b1a7d2: implement minimal toolcache-gating logic + config manifest
- c2f3e8a: add dep-heatmap collector and lightweight telemetry exporter
- 7e12a4f: wire presubmit runner to consult sanitizer decision API; add opt-in env var PRESUBMIT_SANITIZER=on
- 19b5d4c: add integration tests for sanitizer and heatmap in presubmit-sandbox profile
- 0a7b9d1: docs and migration notes (console toggle + Linear tasks)

What presubmit-sanitizer does: single-process HTTP service that receives a summary of changed files and heuristics (language, runtime surface touched, test tags). It returns a minimal execution plan: toolcache buckets to fetch, a narrowed test matrix, and a flag whether to run longtests. The initial heuristics are conservative (fail-open) and controlled via a feature flag. The goal is to reduce average presubmit network I/O by 40% on micro-change diffs and reduce median-turnaround for fast-feedback lanes by ~30%.

What dep-heatmap does: a background job run from the CI telemetry pipeline that correlates dependency changes (package, version) with presubmit/test failures and runtime path coverage (from existing trace sampling). It emits a weekly "heat" score per package and surfaces high-impact candidates in a new dashboard (internal only) and via a small RFC-style JSON artifact attached to CI runs. This helps the dep-rotation team prioritize manual upgrades for packages that actually affect runtime behavior.

Files changed (high level):
- infra/presubmit/sanitizer/ (new service + Dockerfile + Go + minimal CLI)
- infra/presubmit/configs/sanitizer-manifests.yaml (new manifest and feature flags)
- ci/presubmit-runner/main.go (hook to call sanitizer and conditionally change matrix)
- ci/telemetry/dep_heatmap_collector/ (collector + exporter + unit tests)
- docs/engineering/presubmit-sanitizer.md (runbook + rollout steps)
- .github/workflows/presubmit-sandbox.yml (added a sandbox run for new integration smoke)

Example of the sanitizer decision (illustrative snippet added to repo):
- request: {changed_files:["sdk/python/redwood/cli.py","docs/quickstart.md"], language_tags:["python"], test_tags:["unit"]} -> response: {toolcache:["python:3.10:slim"], matrix:["unit"], run_longtests:false} (note: actual request/response is protobuf over HTTP in binary; docs include human readable examples)

Testing and CI: Added a presubmit-sandbox workflow that runs the sanitizer and collector end-to-end in a hermetic environment. CI flakiness surfaced in the first run due to a flaky network stub; fixed by switching to the local mock cache and re-ran. Final CI status: all checks green (lint, unit, integration-sandbox, telemetry-smoke). We intentionally kept the integration matrix small for the first rollout.

Rollout plan: staged behind a feature flag. Default state: off. Rollout phases:
- phase 0: infra teams opt-in to feature flag; run in dry-run mode to collect delta metrics (2 weeks)
- phase 1: opt-in teams enable sanitizer for fast-feedback lanes (4 weeks), compare median turnaround and cache hit rates
- phase 2: enable for all non-blocking PRs, monitor SLOs; fallback path: run-original-matrix when sanitizer service unhealthy

Backward compatibility and failure modes: sanitizer is fail-open: if it fails or returns an invalid decision the presubmit-runner falls back to existing matrix. The toolchain gating is additive (reduces fetches), not removing any artifacts needed for release builds. The dep-heatmap collector only reads CI telemetry and writes internal artifacts; it does not alter builds. No customer-facing API changes.

Review conversation (high level):
- Ben Cook: "Can we ensure the mock cache is deterministic? I saw a nondeterministic file ordering once in the first run."
  - Priya: "Addressed in 4b1a7d2 — switched to sorted filewalk and added a deterministic snapshot for the mock cache."
- Elena Garcia: "Need more observability around sanitizer decisions (why we excluded a test)."
  - Priya: "Added decision.debug log with provenance and a decision_id that ties to telemetry; sanitized PII before emitting."
- Samir Khan: "Heatmap scoring algorithm seems sensitive to baseline noise. Add smoothing and min-sample thresholds."
  - Priya: "Added a rolling-window smoothing (7-day) and require at least 5 correlated failures before surfacing a package as warm/hot."
- Ops (internal comment): "Can we provide a graceful fallback when the sanitizer is upgraded?"
  - Priya: "Added a service-version acceptance header; runner rejects unknown major versions and falls back to classic matrix. Documented in presubmit-sanitizer.md."

Related work & references: Linear ENG-812 (presubmit cost reduction), ENG-813 (dep-rotation prioritization). See RFC: /docs/rfcs/2025-09-presubmit-sanitizer.md and the internal dashboard prototype at telemetry.redwood/internal/dep-heatmap (internal link).

Migration and cleanup tasks included in this PR: a small migration script to add PRESUBMIT_SANITIZER toggle in team repo configs and a one-off job that seeds the first week of heatmap data using a historical CI window. We also created a follow-up Linear task (ENG-879) to widen test coverage for language-specific heuristics and to audit false-negatives.

Merge notes: Squash-merged to main on 2025-11-10 after two rounds of review and CI green. Post-merge: created release candidate tag presubmit-sanitizer-v0.1.0 and updated internal runbook with rollback steps and monitoring dashboards.

If you're reviewing: focus on the sanitizer heuristics file (infra/presubmit/sanitizer/heuristics.go), the runner integration (ci/presubmit-runner/main.go), and the heatmap collector aggregation logic (ci/telemetry/dep_heatmap_collector/aggregator.go). The rest are scaffolding, tests, and docs.

- [x] Docs and runbook for rollout and rollback
- [x] Feature flag for opt-in and dry-run mode
- [x] Deterministic mocks for CI test stability
